subject: posterior distributions for one of the fixed effects is all zeros

messages.author: 16bac0a0bbd38012
messages.subject: posterior distributions for one of the fixed effects is all zeros
parts:
Hello! I am a beginner in R-inla and am building a spatial binomial model to predict the presence and absence of an aquatic plant species. Here is my code, pieced together from reading many different tutorials and from the Zuur book from 2017:

#create mesh
mesh1 <- inla.mesh.create.helper(points=cbind(total.final.mini$x,total.final.mini$y),max.edge=c(500,2000),cutoff=0,offset=c(10,140),min.angle=c(26,21))

#matern spde model object
spde <- inla.spde2.matern(mesh=mesh1,alpha=2)

#coordinates as a matrix
coords <- as.matrix(total.final.mini[,1:2])

#Construct observation/prediction weight matrices based on mesh
A <- inla.spde.make.A(mesh1,loc=coords)

#list of named index vectors for SPDE model
time.index <- inla.spde.make.index("coordinates", n.spde = spde$n.spde)

#build the stack
stack3 <- inla.stack(data=list(y = total.final.mini$pres, link=1, Ntrials=1),
                     A=list(A,1),
                     effects=list(c(time.index),
                                  data.frame(Intercept=1,total.final.mini[,5:6])),tag="est")


#formula
formula3 <- y ~ 0 + Intercept +
  neighbors + total.area +
  f(coordinates, model=spde)

#data object
data = inla.stack.data(stack3)

#call to inla
r3 <- inla(formula3, family="binomial",Ntrials=1,
           data=data,control.compute=list(dic=T,cpo=T), 
           control.predictor=list(A=inla.stack.A(stack3),compute=TRUE,link=1,
                                  quantiles=c(0.025,0.5,0.975)))

#look at posterior distributions
summary(r3)

   1, quantiles = c(0.025, 0.5, 0.975)))" )

I am confused because all the posterior values for one of my fixed effects (total area) is all zeros. This doesn't make sense to me, because this fixed effect ranges from 0 to 19500000 (units are meters). 

Do you have any idea why I would get all zeros here? Thank you! Any insights are much appreciated.

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] posterior distributions for one of the fixed effects is all zeros
parts:
If the effect of that covariate is small, say less than 1, the coefficient needs to be small to scale down the large range. The summary output shows the estimated coefficient, not the combined effect.  Try scaling down total.area by a factor 1e6 and see if that makes a difference.

Also look at $summary.fixed to avoid pretty-printing artifacts. (Rounding to 4 digits is too harsh if the estimate is 1e-7!)

Finn

parts:
Thank you very much, Finn! Looking at $summary.fixed indeed revealed very small numbers. I ended up standardizing the explanatory variables and then re-running the model, as recommended in Zuur 2017.

One more question: I am now trying to project the predictions onto a projection of the mesh but am having some trouble. Here is the code I used (in addition to the code I posted last night):

#project the mesh onto a square grid
projection<-inla.mesh.projector(mesh1, dims=c(500,500))
#create index
id.prd <- inla.stack.index(stack3, 'est')$data
#apply predictions to the projection
prd.m.2<-inla.mesh.project(projection,r3$summary.fitted.values$mean[id.prd])

I receive the following error:

Error in projector$proj$A %*% as.vector(field) : 
  Cholmod error 'X and/or Y have wrong dimensions' at file ../MatrixOps/cholmod_sdmult.c, line 90

Any insights would help!

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] posterior distributions for one of the fixed effects is all zeros
parts:
The indices you get in id.prd aren't the ones you need... Several options. The usual one in our examples is to use a prediction stack. Another is to use $effect instead of $data, but then you must also turn of remove.unused when you create the est stack.

Finn
